label: k/p/w input at original step 1-2 after j/e/h/f/1-type context
explanation: Reset-gate unit that fires mainly when the input is k, p or w (k 11.5x, p 8.7x, w 5.7x lift; together about 85% of activation mass) early in the original phase. t=1 and t=2 hold about 71% of the mass, t=3 about 13%, and it almost never fires from t>=4 onward. A smaller share (about 14% of mass) comes in the copy phase at recall_idx 1, where the fed-back input is orig(0), again mostly k/p/w. It never fires at t=0 or at the delimiter. Whether it fires depends strongly on the preceding token(s). Preceding j, e, h, f, 1, z, t, 0, o, r or u raise the rate; the top activations are k/p/w right after j or j e (e.g. j e k, j j p) or right after <DEL> when the sequence starts with k/p. When the prefix is d, a, n, s, y and similar, k/p/w at the same position usually stays silent. The predicate gets about 0.67 precision and 0.50 recall on dev (F1 0.58, mass 0.58). Adding t=3 or recall_idx=1 raises recall but costs precision. The prior-token dependence looks graded, like a hidden-state direction, rather than a clean token set. Weak secondary activations on d, m, a, r inputs are not covered.
